quickSummary: Secondary growth increases organ girth. Intra-stelar growth occurs via the vascular cambial ring (formed by primary intrafascicular and dedifferentiated interfascicular cambium), producing secondary xylem internally (~10x faster) and secondary phloem externally. Extra-stelar growth occurs via Phellogen (cork cambium), cutting off suberized dead Phellem (cork) externally and living Phelloderm internally: $\text{Periderm} = \text{Phellem} + \text{Phellogen} + \text{Phelloderm}$. Bark comprises all tissues outside the vascular cambium. Lenticels facilitate gas exchange.

conceptBreakdown.title: 7. Secondary Growth in Dicot Stems Overview

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Vascular cambium produces wood (sec. xylem) inside and sec. phloem outside. Phellogen produces Phellem (cork) outside and Phelloderm inside. Bark = Periderm + All Phloem.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SECONDARY GROWTH MECHANISM
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
 INTRA-STELAR SECONDARY GROWTH                            EXTRA-STELAR SECONDARY GROWTH
 (Vascular Cambium Activity)                              (Cork Cambium / Phellogen Activity)
 ├── Cuts off Secondary Xylem (Inside)                    ├── Cuts off Phellem / Cork (Outside)
 └── Cuts off Secondary Phloem (Outside)                  └── Cuts off Phelloderm (Inside)
conceptBreakdown.content: Secondary growth is the increase in lateral girth/diameter of plant organs resulting from the mitotic activity of secondary lateral meristems (Vascular Cambium and Cork Cambium). It occurs in gymnosperms and dicotyledons (*ABSENT in monocotyledons*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.1 Formation & Activity of the Vascular Cambial Ring
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.1 Formation & Activity of the Vascular Cambial Ring
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
VASCULAR CAMBIUM RING FORMATION
                                     │
   Intrafascicular Cambium (Primary) + Interfascicular Cambium (Dedifferentiated Medullary Rays)
                                     │
                                     ▼
                          CONTINUOUS CAMBIAL RING
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
   Inner Side (Centripetal)                                Outer Side (Centrifugal)
   Cuts off **Secondary Xylem (Wood)**                     Cuts off **Secondary Phloem**
   (10x faster activity)                                   (Pushed outward; primary phloem crushed)
conceptBreakdown.content:
### Cambial Ring Assembly
1. **Intrafascicular Cambium**: Primary meristematic strip situated between primary xylem and primary phloem inside open vascular bundles.
2. **Interfascicular Cambium**: Cells of medullary rays adjacent to intrafascicular cambium undergo **dedifferentiation** to become meristematic.
3. **Cambial Ring Activity**: The continuous ring divides periclinally:
   - Cells cut off toward the interior (pith) differentiate into **Secondary Xylem** (accumulates as wood).
   - Cells cut off toward the exterior (cortex) differentiate into **Secondary Phloem**.
   - The cambium is significantly more active on its inner side (~10-fold); hence, secondary xylem accumulates much faster, crushing primary phloem and cortical layers outward.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.2 Extra-Stelar Secondary Growth: The Periderm & Bark
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.2 Extra-Stelar Secondary Growth: The Periderm & Bark
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PERIDERM TISSUE LAYERS
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                           ▼                           ▼
  PHELLEM (Cork)              PHELLOGEN (Cork Cambium)    PHELLODERM (Sec. Cortex)
  Outer suberized dead        Middle secondary lateral     Inner living parenchymatous
  protective layers           meristem layer               storage layers
conceptBreakdown.content:
As secondary xylem expands, the outer cortical and epidermal layers rupture under mechanical tension. To replace the damaged outer envelope, a new secondary lateral meristem called the **Cork Cambium (Phellogen)** develops in the outer cortical region.

### Periderm Formula
$$\Large \mathbf{\text{PERIDERM} = \text{PHELLEM} + \text{PHELLOGEN} + \text{PHELLODERM}}$$

• **Phellem (Cork)**: Cells cut off externally by phellogen. Cells become dead at maturity with walls heavily impregnated with hydrophobic **suberin**, making cork impervious to water and gases.
• **Phelloderm (Secondary Cortex)**: Living parenchymatous cells cut off internally by phellogen.

### Bark Architecture
A non-technical term describing all tissues situated outside the vascular cambium:
$$\Large \mathbf{\text{BARK} = \text{PERIDERM} + \text{PRIMARY \& SECONDARY PHLOEM}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: Lenticel Architecture
conceptBreakdown.title: Lenticel Architecture
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
LENTICEL ARCHITECTURE
                           
    Suberized Phellem ──► Ruptured Epidermis ──► Loose Complementary Cells ──► Phellogen
conceptBreakdown.content: **Lenticels** are lens-shaped aerating openings in the periderm formed when phellogen cuts off loosely arranged, non-suberized parenchymatous cells (**complementary cells**) instead of cork. Lenticels facilitate vital gas exchange between internal stem tissues and the atmosphere.
